solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cook with herb — prescribed amount (6)

blocks.note: to do food is to cook it
a kitchen herb

annotation.surface: A kitchen instruction to cook with a herb, trailing off into a doctor's measured amount.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue: the recipe half is the wordplay, the medical half the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A dosage is the amount of a medicine a doctor prescribes.

entries.clue: Maybe the Sixties baddy plunged into river (6)

indicatorNotes.plunged into: the baddy is plunged into the river, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Scotland and in England/Wales
a cad is a man who behaves badly

annotation.surface: A villain from the Sixties thrown into a river.
annotation.walkthrough: "Maybe" marks the Sixties as one example of the answer, a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sixties are a decade, a period of ten years.

entries.clue: Plays out (6,7)

blocks.note: the surface reads a verb, as in events playing out; the setter means stage plays, a noun
not unfolding but outdoors: plays staged out in the open

annotation.walkthrough: "Plays out" reads as a verb, as in events playing out; read it as nouns, plays that are performed outside.
annotation.definitionFit: Street theatre is drama put on outdoors in public spaces.

entries.clue: Derbyshire town starts to seem sticky with viscous liquid around (7)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the next words are taken
indicatorNotes.around: the gloop goes around those letters

blocks.note: gloop is thick, sticky liquid
first letters of seem and sticky

annotation.surface: A town where everything seems coated in something thick and sticky.
annotation.walkthrough: The pair of starting letters sits between the two Os. Glossop is a market town in the Peak District of Derbyshire, England.
annotation.definitionFit: Glossop is a town in the High Peak area of Derbyshire.

entries.clue: Sailor with a rod wandering about on ship (6)

indicatorNotes.wandering about: letters that wander about are moved out of order

blocks.note: AB, able seaman
A ROD rearranged

annotation.surface: A sailor strolling round the deck carrying a fishing rod.
annotation.walkthrough: AB, able seaman, is the standard crossword sailor. "About" belongs with "wandering", leaving "on ship" as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a passenger who is aboard is on the ship.

entries.clue: Like scientific establishment set up in wood (5)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up turns the letters to read upwards

blocks.note: as = like
a laboratory

annotation.surface: A research lab being set up in a forest.
annotation.walkthrough: AS + LAB, then the whole lot runs upwards to give BALSA.
annotation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood used for models.

entries.clue: One’s charged leading character, quiet leader? (5,8)

annotation.definitionNote: read as "one that is charged", a noun

blocks.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet
p, piano, quiet in music
a leader is a newspaper's leading article, its editorial

annotation.surface: Someone charged with an offence who is a leading figure yet a quiet leader.
annotation.walkthrough: "Charged" suggests a criminal charge; here it is electric charge. In Britain a newspaper's leader is its editorial, the leading article.
annotation.definitionFit: An alpha particle carries a positive electric charge.

entries.clue: Led astray, eating strange piece of cake! (6)

indicatorNotes.astray: letters led astray are moved out of order
indicatorNotes.eating: the rearranged letters eat, so hold, the next piece

blocks.note: LED rearranged
odd = strange

annotation.surface: Someone lured into eating a strange bit of cake.
annotation.walkthrough: "Piece of cake" looks like food in the surface; it is the definition. A doddle is British slang for an easy task.
annotation.definitionFit: A piece of cake and a doddle both mean something very easy.

entries.clue: Goods vehicle departs (7)

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
goes = departs

annotation.surface: A goods lorry pulling away.
annotation.walkthrough: "Goods vehicle" reads as one phrase, a lorry; split it after Goods, which is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cargoes are goods carried by ship, plane or lorry.

entries.clue: Cameras shot holy books in religious ceremony (9)

indicatorNotes.shot: something shot is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: CAMERAS rearranged
NT, the New Testament

annotation.surface: Photographers snapping the holy books during a church service.
annotation.walkthrough: "Shot" suggests photography alongside cameras; here it means wrecked.
annotation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a religious ceremony such as baptism or communion.

entries.clue: Was first to get outside work and made great strides? (5)

indicatorNotes.to get outside: the first word's letters go outside the next

blocks.note: to lead is to be first
op, opus, a work

annotation.surface: A runner who got out in front early and strode away.
annotation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the standard crossword work, and the question mark admits that loping is only loosely great strides.
annotation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy strides.

entries.clue: Clothes carried by laundresses (5)

indicatorNotes.carried by: the answer is carried inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle, after LAUN and before ES

annotation.surface: Washerwomen carrying the laundry.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is already hiding in the washerwomen's name, which fits a clue about clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective noun: dress means clothing in general, as in evening dress.

entries.clue: Drink, something bitter for painter (7)

blocks.note: cha, char, British slang for tea
gall, bile, is proverbially bitter

annotation.surface: A bitter drink handed to an artist.
annotation.walkthrough: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter.
annotation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a twentieth-century painter.

entries.clue: Ban a panto — naughty leading comedian (3,6)

indicatorNotes.naughty: naughty letters misbehave and fall out of order

blocks.note: BAN A PANTO rearranged

annotation.surface: A call to ban a pantomime because its star comic is too rude.
annotation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas family show full of slapstick. Top banana is American slang for the star comic of a show.
annotation.definitionFit: Top banana is old vaudeville slang for the lead comedian on the bill.

entries.clue: Avoid drink? Don’t commit to a view (7)

blocks.note: to go without alcohol, as a teetotaller does
what a voter does who backs neither side

annotation.surface: Advice to stay sober and to sit on the fence.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that avoiding drink is only one kind of refraining; the voting sense is the second meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Abstaining means both refusing drink and declining to vote either way.

entries.clue: For the most part, put up with school soup (6)

indicatorNotes.For the most part: most of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.clueFragment: For the most part, put up with
blocks.note: BORE, put up with, minus its last letter
SCH, abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: Someone mostly tolerating the soup served at school dinners.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put up with" is BORE, as in bore the pain; losing its last letter leaves BOR.
annotation.definitionFit: Borsch is an Eastern European beetroot soup.

entries.clue: Finish after day five as main man? (6)

blocks.note: Friday, the fifth day of the working week
end = finish

annotation.surface: Wrapping up on day five of a Test match as the star player.
annotation.walkthrough: "After" puts the finish after the day. Main man is slang for a best friend; the question mark flags the loose fit.
annotation.definitionFit: Your main man is your closest friend.

entries.clue: Supervise, as a bishop (7)

blocks.note: to manage and watch over work
what a bishop does to a diocese; the word bishop comes from Greek episkopos

annotation.walkthrough: The second half describes what a bishop does: the Greek episkopos, source of bishop, means overseer, and a bishop's district is his see.
annotation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, which is a bishop's job.

entries.clue: Plant with two names found in salt water (5)

indicatorNotes.found in: the names are found inside the water

blocks.note: the sea is salt water
N is short for name, twice

annotation.surface: A plant with two botanical names growing in seawater.
annotation.walkthrough: "Two names" hints at a botanical Latin name; it is just N twice.
annotation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant whose pods are used as a laxative.

entries.clue: Instrument with which celebrity enthrals India (5)

indicatorNotes.enthrals: to enthral is to hold captive, so the celebrity holds India

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity
I is India in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A famous musician whose playing captivates India.
annotation.walkthrough: I goes inside STAR, after the S. The sitar fits the Indian scene the surface paints.
annotation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.

entries.clue: Posed wearing fine material (5)

blocks.note: a model sat, or posed, for a painter
in = wearing, as in dressed in blue

annotation.surface: A model posing in a fine fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wearing" looks like a verb about the model; here it is IN, as in a woman in red.
annotation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, glossy fabric.

entries.clue: Sleeplike state, having eaten hot portion (7)

indicatorNotes.having eaten: the state has eaten the letter, so holds it inside

blocks.note: a trance is a sleeplike state
H, hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone dozing off after eating a hot helping.
annotation.walkthrough: H goes inside TRANCE, before the final E.
annotation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice, often of money.

entries.clue: Wild animals — any he’s found roaming? (6)

indicatorNotes.roaming: roaming letters wander out of order

blocks.note: ANY HES rearranged

annotation.surface: Asking whether any males are out roaming among the wild animals.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in "he's" is ignored, as punctuation always is in anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyenas are wild carnivores of Africa and Asia.

entries.clue: Really popular exploit (6)

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
a deed is a feat or exploit

annotation.surface: A truly popular heroic feat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Really" looks like an intensifier for popular; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Indeed and really both express emphasis or surprise.
